question: We are about to deploy a Soroban contract that will hold user funds to Mainnet. What security steps and tools does SDF recommend first?

golden.answer: As of 2026-11-14 SDF's guidance is: write a threat model (Stellar Docs has a STRIDE guide and template) and a monitoring plan; run analysis tools such as Scout (static analysis) and Certora Sunbeam (formal verification); get a third-party audit before accepting material user funds, through the Audit Bank if SCF-funded; and deploy exactly the audited code, from a verifiable build.
keyFacts: Stellar Docs provide a threat modeling guide with a STRIDE template.
SDF lists Scout for static analysis and Certora Sunbeam for formal verification.
SDF expects a completed third-party audit before material user funds are accepted.
The code deployed to Mainnet should be the code that was audited.
avoid: Do NOT say an audit alone makes a contract safe to deploy.
golden.notes: The tool roster is dated; accept other SDF-listed tools such as Almanax, the OpenZeppelin detectors, or Komet. Accept bug bounties, multisig admin keys, pause controls, and incident response as further SDF recommendations; do not require them.

truth.notes: The audit and parity expectations come from SDF's 2026-07-20 post, which addresses DeFi protocols that touch user funds; the question is scoped to a contract holding user funds for that reason. The Security Tools page listed four tools on 2026-11-14: Scout: Bug Fighter, Almanax, Certora Sunbeam and the Soroban Security Portal. The stellar-dev-skill security.md adds the OpenZeppelin Security Detectors SDK, Komet and OpenZeppelin Monitor. Audit Bank partner-firm rosters differ between the 2024 launch post, the current page and the skill; no roster is pinned. One parallel-cli research run (core-fast, 2026-11-14) reproduced all four facts and flagged only that roster difference. Boundary: q-soroban-vuln-classes and q-soroban-reentrancy test vulnerability classes; q-scf-audit-bank tests the Audit Bank's terms.

sources.quote: A series of guides and documentation to help developers build safe and secure products on Stellar.
STRIDE Threat Model Template: Use this template to create a STRIDE threat model for your project.
On-Chain Monitoring Plan Template (Builders): For Builders - turn your threat model into a monitoring plan
A static code analysis tool built to assist Soroban developers and auditors in identifying potential security threats
Sunbeam is a formal verification tool developed by Certora for Soroban smart contracts on the Stellar blockchain.
A completed audit before any material user funds are accepted, conducted by a firm with a demonstrated track record (published 2026-07-20)
Audit-to-deployment parity. The code running in production should be the code that was reviewed.
Audits are necessary but not sufficient.
Ship the deploy through a verified build so the on-chain WASM hash traces back to a reviewable commit.
Before requesting an audit: run the static analyzers, complete the checklists above, document your threat model and trust assumptions
The Soroban Security Audit Bank provides comprehensive, structured security audits for eligible projects funded through the Stellar Community Fund
published July 20, 2026 (author: Justin Rice) … Flags / disagreements: (a) Audit Bank partner firms differ by source

corroboration.claim: Stellar Docs provide a threat modeling guide with a STRIDE template, and a monitoring plan template that builds on the threat model.

evidence.note: Lists the how-to guide, the STRIDE template and a worked example.
Builder template turns the threat model into a monitoring plan.
SDF's skill tells teams to document the threat model and trust assumptions before requesting an audit.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-11-14 SDF lists Scout for static analysis and Certora Sunbeam for formal verification among its security tools.

evidence.note: Both tools have entries on the Security Tools page.
The Tooling section lists Scout under static analysis and Certora Sunbeam under formal verification.
Independent run listed the same tools from the same page.

corroboration.claim: SDF expects a completed third-party audit before material user funds are accepted, and the deployed code to be the audited code.

evidence.note: Section 'Security audits that actually mean something': completed audit before material user funds, and audit-to-deployment parity.
'Before mainnet' requires a verified build so the on-chain WASM traces to a reviewable commit.
Dated independent summary of the post (July 20, 2026): audits before user funds, bug bounties, emergency pause controls.

corroboration.claim: SDF states that an audit is necessary but not sufficient.

evidence.note: 'An audit is a point-in-time snapshot' and 'Audits are necessary but not sufficient.'
The checklist adds emergency controls, an incident runbook and a gated, tested upgrade path beyond the audit.

evidence: Sibling sweep: q-soroban-vuln-classes, q-soroban-reentrancy, q-soroban-fuzz-testing, q-soroban-instance-storage-dos and q-scf-audit-bank do not test pre-Mainnet practice and do not contradict it.
